meta.headline: **Partial implementation (B)** is the dominant outcome, and Antigua and Barbuda submitted a detailed National Report: the High Court decriminalised consensual same-sex relations in July 2022 (**A**, though the provisions were not formally repealed), ILO Conventions 190 and 183 were ratified in 2022, maternity leave rose to 14 weeks, a National Child Protection Policy (2021), a Sexual Offenders Registry (2022), a GBV Action Plan (2023), a shelter partnership, prison upgrades, higher pensions (2025-2026) and large climate-resilience financing were reported. **No relevant action (C)** persists on the unratified treaties and protocols (ICPPED, OP-CAT, the Second Optional Protocol), a national human rights institution, a national reporting mechanism, anti-discrimination legislation, criminalisation of marital rape, abortion, corporal punishment in schools and formal abolition of the death penalty (a de facto moratorium since 1991). No trafficking conviction has ever been secured.

Step up activities to address the problem of extreme overcrowding in the country’s prison facility
Improve the conditions of detention facilities, including hygiene and sanitation
Ensure that places of detention comply with the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners
Take additional measures to improve the conditions of detention of prisoners
Bring its prisons into line with the Nelson Mandela Rules

blocks.summary: Commission a State report on prison conditions
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Commission a State report into prison conditions in order to ascertain the quality of the detention facilities and as a means to measure future improvements

blocks.summary: Ratify other instruments
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on these instruments.

recommendations.text: Implement the Government’s proposal for fighting corruption domestically and in the Caribbean and address recommendations received through the Mechanism for Follow-up on the Implementation of the Inter-American Convention against Corruption peer review process

themes.theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery

blocks.summary: Strengthen anti-trafficking measures and victim assistance
blocks.rationale: A Trafficking in Persons Prevention Unit investigates cases (13 suspects in 2024), a 2025 National Action Plan exists and victims receive services; no conviction has ever been secured.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 37 — Antigua and Barbuda: "the Trafficking in Persons Prevention Unit initiated investigations of 13 suspects in nine cases"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/3), para. 7 — ECLJ: "no individual had ever been convicted of human trafficking in Antigua and Barbuda and no victim had been formally identified"

recommendations.text: Strengthen measures to assist victims of human trafficking, taking into account the needs of particularly vulnerable groups such as women domestic workers
Strengthen the local Trafficking in Persons Prevention Committee in order to completely halt any form of human trafficking
Continue to allocate sufficient resources to programmes on combating trafficking in persons, and provide adequate services to victims to support their reintegration and rehabilitation
Intensify efforts to prevent trafficking and sexual exploitation of women and girls
Continue efforts to combat trafficking in persons and to prevent all forms of slavery

blocks.summary: Implement anti-slavery legislation
blocks.rationale: There has never been a conviction for trafficking.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/3), para. 7 — ECLJ: "no individual had ever been convicted of human trafficking in Antigua and Barbuda"

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Implement legislation to address modern slavery and human trafficking, and expedite current cases by providing adequate resources and training for officials to effectively investigate and prosecute cases and protect victims

blocks.summary: Remove exceptions to the minimum age of marriage
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Amend the Marriage Act to remove exceptions that allow marriage for those under the age of 18 years

blocks.summary: Social programmes and poverty alleviation
blocks.rationale: The HAPPI housing programme has delivered 111 homes, pensions were raised in 2025 and 2026 and food assistance continues.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 39 — Antigua and Barbuda: "The programme has delivered 111 homes across the island so far"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 43 — Antigua and Barbuda: "In April 2025, the Government increased the minimum pension payable from EC$350.00 to EC$500"

recommendations.text: Sustain efforts to alleviate poverty and strengthen the social protection system
Continue to prioritize social programmes, with an emphasis on eradicating and alleviating poverty
Continue to promote its successful social policies in the areas of education, health and poverty reduction, for the benefit of the most vulnerable groups

blocks.summary: Allocate more resources to social protection
blocks.rationale: The National Social Protection Act 2020 exists and minimum pensions were raised in 2025 and 2026.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 43 — Antigua and Barbuda: "In 2026, a 5% increase in payments for pensioners across the board through the ABSSS was approved"

recommendations.text: Deepen efforts to allocate more resources to social protection

blocks.summary: Promote sustainable development and living standards
blocks.rationale: Housing, renewable energy and resilience-financing programmes were launched.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 49 — Antigua and Barbuda: "The Government continues to promote climate-adaptive development through the Sustainable Island Resource Framework Fund"

recommendations.text: Continue to promote sustainable economic and social development, and to improve people’s living standards, so as to lay a solid foundation for people’s enjoyment of human rights

blocks.summary: Decriminalise consensual same-sex relations
blocks.rationale: The High Court struck down sections 12 and 15 of the Sexual Offences Act in July 2022, decriminalising consensual same-sex relations; the provisions have not been formally repealed by legislation.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 17 — Antigua and Barbuda: "striking down sections 12 and 15 of the Sexual Offences Act of 1995, which criminalised same-sex sexual relations and ascribed custodial criminal sentences"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 52 — United Nations country team: "had not been formally repealed by legislative amendment, but rather rendered unenforceable through the Court’s declaration of unconstitutionality"

recommendations.text: Decriminalize the voluntary interruption of pregnancy and expand its admitted grounds, particularly in cases of sexual abuse or high-risk pregnancies

Consider legalizing abortion in cases of rape, incest, threats to the life or health of the pregnant woman and severe fetal impairment; decriminalize it in all other cases; and ensure access for women to safe, high-quality and affordable abortion-related care, including post-abortion care in cases of complications resulting from unsafe abortions
Legalize abortion in certain cases such as rape, incest and serious malformation of the fetus, and decriminalize it in all other cases

blocks.summary: Decriminalise abortion
blocks.rationale: Abortion remains criminalised except where the pregnant woman's life is at risk.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 29 — United Nations country team: "abortion remained criminalized in Antigua and Barbuda under the Offences Against the Person Act, except in limited circumstances where the continuation of pregnancy posed a risk to the life of the pregnant woman"

recommendations.text: Amend its legislation in order to legalize the termination of pregnancies in cases of risk to the life of the pregnant woman, rape, incest and severe impairment of the fetus
Form a legislative committee to revise the abortion law to allow the termination of pregnancy

blocks.summary: Strengthen health-care access and resources
blocks.rationale: A dedicated NCD department, free HPV cervical cancer screening, a planned renal centre and a 2026 transition to national health insurance advance access.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 46 — Antigua and Barbuda: "Women between the ages of 30 and 65 in Antigua and Barbuda are eligible for free HPV Cervical Cancer screening"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 28 — United Nations country team: "the scheme would be transformed into a national health insurance scheme in 2026"

recommendations.text: Continue strengthening measures to ensure access to health care by allocating adequate resources in the health sector, especially for the treatment of non-communicable diseases
Continue to improve the health-care system with measures to allocate more resources and upgrade infrastructure, in order to strengthen maternal health

themes.theme: Human rights education, trainings & awareness raising

blocks.summary: Revise the Health and Family Life Education curriculum
blocks.rationale: No comprehensive sexuality education aligned with international guidance has been implemented.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/3), para. 10 — JS1: "no comprehensive sexuality education in line with international standards had been implemented"

recommendations.text: Revise the Health and Family Life Education Programme curriculum in line with the United Nations technical guidelines, and train teachers to ensure effective provision of the curriculum

blocks.summary: Integrate children with disabilities in regular schools
blocks.rationale: The Ministry of Education is training specialist teachers and screening children to integrate them in the broader school network.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 55 — Antigua and Barbuda: "continues to work toward integrating children with disabilities into the broader school network"

recommendations.text: Integrate children with disabilities in regular schools by giving particular attention to the training of specialists for children with intellectual and psychological disabilities

blocks.summary: Comprehensive sexuality education
blocks.rationale: No comprehensive sexuality education in line with international standards has been implemented.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/3), para. 10 — JS1: "no comprehensive sexuality education in line with international standards had been implemented"

recommendations.text: Ensure comprehensive sexuality education, with a view to preventing teenage pregnancies and the spread of sexually transmitted infections, in particular HIV
Ensure comprehensive sexuality education, with a view to preventing teenage pregnancies and the spread of sexually transmitted infections, in particular HIV

blocks.summary: Resource education initiatives and invest in education
blocks.rationale: Public education is free, CSEC examination fees are covered (2026) and tertiary education is tuition-free; comprehensive sexuality education has not been implemented.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 68 — Antigua and Barbuda: "have also been made tuitionfree by the Government"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/3), para. 10 — JS1: "no comprehensive sexuality education in line with international standards had been implemented"

recommendations.text: Continue to provide adequate resources towards the initiatives that have started to help teenage mothers finish their secondary school education, in classes that can accommodate the unique challenges of being a young single mother
Further increase investment in education and improve the enrolment rate of children in schools

blocks.summary: Strengthen laws and policies against sexual and gender-based violence
blocks.rationale: The Workplace Violence and Harassment (Prevention) Bill is before Parliament, a Sexual Offenders Registry was created (2022) and a model Sexual Offences Court operates; marital rape is not fully criminalised.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 78 — Antigua and Barbuda: "Parliament is presently tabling the Workplace Violence and Harassment (Prevention) Bill"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 49 — United Nations country team: "marital rape was not fully criminalized in all circumstances under section 3 (1) of the Sexual Offences Act"

recommendations.text: Pass legislation explicitly defining and prohibiting sexual harassment in the public and private sectors, with protections against retaliation for those who report
Take all the necessary measures to strengthen the fight against gender-based violence, and in particular sexual violence

blocks.summary: Criminalise marital rape
blocks.rationale: Marital rape is not fully criminalised.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 49 — United Nations country team: "marital rape was not fully criminalized in all circumstances under section 3 (1) of the Sexual Offences Act"

recommendations.text: Step up the fight against gender-based violence and sexual violence, and classify marital rape as a crime in the Sexual Offences Act

blocks.summary: Adopt a national gender policy
blocks.rationale: A National Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Policy has a final draft awaiting Cabinet approval.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 64 — Antigua and Barbuda: "A final draft of the policy document has been prepared and is expected to be presented to the Cabinet for approval"

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Develop, adopt and implement, in a consultative manner, a national gender policy with measures for the prevention of sexual and gender-based violence against all women, girls, men and boys, regardless of legal or migratory status, nationality, gender identity or sexual orientation

blocks.summary: Promote women's empowerment and participation
blocks.rationale: Women's representation rose (two women elected to the House in 2026, seven senators) and the Directorate of Gender Affairs runs empowerment programmes; a national gender equality policy is still in final draft.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 9 — Antigua and Barbuda: "The results of the general election saw the election of two female members of the House of Representatives"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 64 — Antigua and Barbuda: "A final draft of the policy document has been prepared and is expected to be presented to the Cabinet for approval"

recommendations.text: Take further steps to promote women’s empowerment in political and public life
Continue strengthening gender equality programmes with concrete measures to consolidate women’s empowerment
Further strengthen gender mainstreaming into national development strategies, and ensure the participation of women and relevant stakeholders in programme planning and implementation

Intensify the measures adopted to promote the empowerment of women, by strengthening the national mechanism for women and the Directorate of Gender Affairs and developing intersectoral monitoring and coordination mechanisms for the implementation of the policies adopted
Intensify efforts to enhance awareness among women of their rights under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
Continue efforts to end all forms of discrimination and violence against women and girls, enshrine gender equality and support women’s empowerment

blocks.summary: Temporary special measures for women
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Take temporary special measures aimed at achieving substantive equality between women and men in all areas where women are underrepresented or disadvantaged, including the political and public spheres, education, employment and health

blocks.summary: Adopt a national gender policy
blocks.rationale: A National Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Policy has a final draft awaiting Cabinet approval.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 64 — Antigua and Barbuda: "A final draft of the policy document has been prepared and is expected to be presented to the Cabinet for approval"

recommendations.text: Continue its effort to promote gender equality by pursuing the development of a national gender policy

blocks.summary: Public policies against gender-based violence
blocks.rationale: A GBV Action Plan (2023), the SARC and a Cabinet-approved shelter partnership advance the policy recommendation; no temporary special measures are reported.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 60 — Antigua and Barbuda: "In 2023, the Directorate developed a new Gender Based Violence Action Plan"

recommendations.text: Develop public policies to combat gender-based violence, in accordance with Sustainable Development Goal 5, and develop temporary special measures to achieve substantive equality, including in political and public life and in access to education, employment and health

blocks.summary: Prevent violence against women and girls
blocks.rationale: The SARC one-stop centre, a police Special Victims Support Unit, a 2023 GBV Action Plan and a Cabinet-approved shelter partnership exist; the national action plan was never formally endorsed and GBV remains pervasive.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 60 — Antigua and Barbuda: "In 2023, the Directorate developed a new Gender Based Violence Action Plan"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 45 — United Nations country team: "the plan was never formally endorsed by the relevant national authorities"

recommendations.text: Continue its efforts to eliminate gender-based violence

Continue to strengthen measures intended to eliminate all forms of violence and ill-treatment of girls and women, including the development of programmes and the provision of training for law enforcement officers on the areas of domestic violence and sexual violence

blocks.summary: Awareness-raising on the death penalty
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on awareness-raising on the death penalty.

recommendations.text: Take further measures to prevent violence against women and girls, including domestic violence, also through awareness-raising campaigns and increased support to victims

blocks.summary: Prohibit corporal punishment of children
blocks.rationale: The Education Act 2008 allows corporal punishment in schools; only its use as a judicial sentence is prohibited.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 14 — UNESCO: "the Education Act of 2008 allowed for the use of corporal punishment in schools (article 50 (2))"

recommendations.text: Explicitly repeal the common-law right to punish children and prohibit all corporal punishment enacted in all settings where adults have authority over children, as previously recommended
Prohibit corporal punishment of children in all settings
Consider undertaking the necessary legislative reforms to prohibit corporal punishment inflicted on children, and continue to promote the use of positive discipline

Carry out the necessary legislative adjustments to explicitly repeal the right to inflict corporal punishment and the sentence of life imprisonment for persons under 18 years of age, in accordance with international human rights standards and target 16.2 of the Sustainable Development Goals
Prohibit corporal punishment of children in all settings
Strengthen measures that specifically prohibit corporal punishment of boys and girls
Take steps to comprehensively address the issue of corporal punishment of children, in particular in schools

blocks.summary: Strengthen child protection institutions and legislation
blocks.rationale: Antigua and Barbuda adopted a National Child Protection Policy (2021), reformed juvenile justice (Child Justice Act 2015, amended 2018) and reopened a rehabilitation centre (2025); corporal punishment remains lawful in schools.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 50 — United Nations country team: "had adopted the National Child Protection Policy (2021)"

National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 69 — Antigua and Barbuda: "The Child Justice (Amendment) Act 2018 also brought significant reform, shifting the age of criminal responsibility from 8 to 12 years of age"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/2), para. 14 — UNESCO: "the Education Act of 2008 allowed for the use of corporal punishment in schools (article 50 (2))"

recommendations.text: Continue strengthening the institutions responsible for the education and protection of children, particularly those with disabilities
Continue efforts to strengthen the legislative framework for child protection and children’s justice
Implement measures to ensure that children in vulnerable areas are not marginalized

blocks.summary: Children's budget and rights-monitoring mechanism
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Seek to conduct a comprehensive assessment of budgetary needs for children, and increase the allocation of financial means to social sectors, education and health to an adequate level

blocks.summary: Mandate to promote and protect women's rights
blocks.rationale: No independent mandate has been established; the Directorate of Gender Affairs is a government department.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 58 — Antigua and Barbuda: "holds the primary mandate in Antigua and Barbuda for mainstreaming"

recommendations.text: Establish an independent mechanism for monitoring children’s rights

themes.theme: Persons with disabilities: definition, general principles

blocks.summary: Strengthen the Disabilities and Equal Opportunities Act
blocks.rationale: The Act (2017) establishes a rights framework and a complaints tribunal; the regulations are outstanding.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/ATG/1), para. 57 — Antigua and Barbuda: "This Act sets out the rights framework for persons living with disabilities and establishes a specialised tribunal for complaints"

recommendations.text: Advance efforts in the drafting of regulations regarding the Disabilities and Equal Opportunities Act
Accelerate drafting of the clarifying regulations required for the Disabilities and Equal Opportunities Act (Georgia).
